text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two Namibian companies are planning to set up a full-scale sealing industry at Henties Bay, which will process and market products made from thousands of seals killed each year along Namibia's coast.

- The Kxoe community are weighing up their options, including the possibility of legal action, in the wake of a government order that they must vacate their community-operated tourism sites in West Caprivi.
- Swapo parliamentarian Angelika Muharukua yesterday criticised the visit of two Himba chiefs to Europe to publicise opposition to the proposed Epupa dam project.
- The financial crisis the fishing industry finds itself in because of the drastic reduction in quotas and poor catches has led to a new fishing giant being established in Namibia.

- The renewed flare-up of fighting in Angola has already spilled over into Namibia after 217 Angolans, who spent months in custody in Namibia prisons, were deported and immediately conscripted into the Angolan defence force.

- As opposition against the proposed Epupa hydropower scheme continues, Nampower has sounded the alarm that it is faced with one of the toughest challenges in the history of power generation in Namibia due to the current historic low level of the Kunene River.
